title.zh: 卷一百五十六 列傳第一百〇六: 于頔 韓弘 王智興
title.en: Volume 156 Biographies 106: Yu Di, Han Hong, Wang Zhixing
title.raw: 卷一百五十六 列傳第一百〇六: 于頔 韓弘 王智興 Volume 156 Biographies 106: Yu Di, Han Hong, Wang Zhixing

sentences.zh: 于頔，字允元，河南人也，周太師燕文公謹之後也。

translations.literal: Yu Di, style name Yun'yuan, was a native of Henan and a descendant of Yan Duke Wen of Zhou, the Grand Preceptor Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di, whose courtesy name was Yun'yuan, came from Henan and was descended from Shen, the Zhou Grand Preceptor enfeoffed as Duke Wen of Yan.

sentences.zh: 始以廕補千牛，調授華陰尉，黜陟使劉灣辟為判官。

translations.literal: At first he entered office through yin privilege as a Thousand-Ox [guard], was transferred and appointed Hua Yin district magistrate, and was recruited as a magistrate's aide by the Inspection Commissioner Liu Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service through hereditary privilege as a guard in the Thousand-Ox regiment, was then assigned as magistrate of Hua Yin, and was recruited as aide by the inspection commissioner Liu Wan.

sentences.zh: 又以櫟陽主簿攝監察御史，充入蕃使判官。

translations.literal: He also served as acting surveillance censor while holding the post of Liyang chief clerical officer, and served as aide to the envoy entering the western regions.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as surveillance censor while chief clerk at Liyang, and acted as aide to an envoy to the western borderlands.

sentences.zh: 再遷司門員外郎，兼侍御史，賜紫。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Gate Office, concurrently serving as attendant censor, and was granted the purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Gate Office, also serving as attendant censor, and was awarded the purple robe of high rank.

sentences.zh: 充入西蕃計會使，將命稱旨，時論以為有出疆專對之能。

translations.literal: He served as accountant for the embassy to the western Tibetans; he carried out his orders to satisfaction, and public opinion held that he possessed the ability to represent the state alone beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: As accountant on an embassy to the western regions, he carried out his commission to the court's satisfaction, and contemporaries judged him capable of representing the dynasty abroad on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 歷長安縣令、駕部郎中。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of magistrate of Chang'an county and Director of the Bureau of Imperial Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Chang'an County and as director in the Bureau of Imperial Transport.

sentences.zh: 出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out [from the capital] and became Prefect of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as prefect of Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 因行縣至長城方山，其下有水曰西湖，南朝疏鑿，溉田三千頃，久堙廢。

translations.literal: While making the rounds of the counties he came to Fang Mountain in Changcheng; below it was a body of water called West Lake, which the Southern Dynasties had dredged and opened, irrigating three thousand qing of fields, but it had long lain silted up and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: On a tour of the counties he came to Fang Mountain at Changcheng, where a body of water called West Lake lay. The Southern Dynasties had once dredged it to irrigate three thousand qing of fields, but it had long been silted up and left unused.

sentences.zh: 頔命設堤塘以復之，歲獲粳稻蒲魚之利，人賴以濟。

translations.literal: Di ordered dikes and ponds built to restore it; each year they obtained the benefits of upland rice, cattails, and fish, and the people relied on this for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Di ordered dikes and ponds built to restore the lake, and each year the region gained rice, cattail, and fish; the people depended on it for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 州境陸地褊狹，其送終者往往不掩其棺槥，頔葬朽骨凡十餘所。

translations.literal: The prefecture's land was narrow and cramped; those conducting funerals often did not cover their coffins, and Di buried decayed bones at more than ten places in all.
translations.idiomatic: Land in the prefecture was scarce, and many burials went without proper covering of the coffins; Di gave decent burial to exposed remains at more than a dozen sites.

sentences.zh: 改蘇州刺史，浚溝瀆，整街衢，至今賴之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Su Prefecture, dredged canals and ditches, and straightened streets and lanes; to this day they rely on this.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Suzhou, he dredged canals and ditches and repaired the streets—a legacy the city still benefits from.

sentences.zh: 吳俗事鬼，頔疾其淫祀廢生業，神宇皆撤去，唯吳太伯、伍員等三數廟存焉。

translations.literal: Wu custom worshipped spirits; Di was vexed that excessive sacrifices disrupted livelihood, had all spirit halls removed, and only a few temples such as those of Taibo of Wu and Wu Yuan were left standing.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu were devoted to spirit cults; Di, distressed that lavish rites were ruining livelihoods, had most shrines demolished, retaining only a handful, including those of Taibo of Wu and Wu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 雖為政有績，然橫暴已甚，追憾湖州舊尉，封杖以計強決之。

translations.literal: Although his governance had achievements, his brutality was already extreme; he harbored resentment against the former Hu prefecture assistant, sealed off beating staffs, and by stratagem forcibly brought the case to judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Though his administration had real accomplishments, his brutality was already extreme; nursing a grudge against a former assistant in Huzhou, he used sealed beating staffs and forced a verdict by coercion.

sentences.zh: 觀察使王緯奏其事，德宗不省。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner Wang Wei memorialized the matter, but Dezong paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Wang Wei reported the affair, but Emperor Dezong took no notice.

sentences.zh: 及後頔累遷，乃與緯書曰：「一蒙惡奏，三度改官。」

translations.literal: After Di had been promoted several times, he wrote to Wei saying: "Once slandered by a malicious memorial, I was transferred three times."
translations.idiomatic: After Di had risen through several promotions, he wrote to Wei: "One malicious memorial cost me three transfers."

sentences.zh: 由大理卿遷陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: From Grand Court Judge he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from Grand Court Judge to surveillance commissioner of Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 自以為得志，益恣威虐。

translations.literal: He considered himself to have attained his ambition and became all the more arbitrary in his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had finally arrived, he indulged his cruelty all the more.

sentences.zh: 官吏日加科罰，其惴恐重足一跡。

translations.literal: Day by day he added fines and punishments on officials; they were fearful and dared not set both feet on the ground at once.
translations.idiomatic: He piled fines and punishments on his staff daily until they lived in terror, scarcely daring to move.

sentences.zh: 掾姚峴不勝其虐，與其弟泛舟於河，遂自投而死。

translations.literal: The aide Yao Xian could not endure his cruelty; he and his younger brother went boating on the river and threw themselves in to die.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Yao Xian, unable to bear the abuse, took his younger brother boating on the river and drowned them both.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，為襄州刺史，充山南東道節度觀察。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he became Prefect of Xiang Prefecture and served as Military Governor and Surveillance Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 798 he became prefect of Xiangzhou and military governor and surveillance commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 地與蔡州鄰。

translations.literal: His territory bordered Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His territory bordered Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠之叛，頔率兵赴唐州，收吳房、朗山縣，又破賊於濯神溝。

translations.literal: When Wu Shao-cheng rebelled, Di led troops to Tang Prefecture, recovered Wu Fang and Langshan counties, and again defeated the rebels at Zhuoshen Ditch.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaocheng rebelled, Di led troops to Tangzhou, recovered Wu Fang and Langshan counties, and routed the rebels at Zhuoshen Ditch.

sentences.zh: 於是廣軍籍，募戰士，器甲犀利，僴然專有漢南之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he expanded the military registers, recruited warriors, and made weapons and armor sharp; he stood aloof and exclusively held the lands south of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: He then expanded his rolls, recruited fighters, and sharpened his armory until he held the Han River southlands as his private domain.

sentences.zh: 小失意者，皆以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Those who suffered even slight displeasure were all dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who crossed him even slightly was punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 因請升襄州為大都督府，府比鄆、魏。

translations.literal: He therefore requested that Xiang Prefecture be elevated to a great metropolitan prefecture, its status comparable to Yan and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to elevate Xiangzhou to a great metropolitan prefecture on a par with Yan and Wei.

sentences.zh: 時德宗方姑息方鎮，聞頔事狀，亦無可奈何，但允順而已。

translations.literal: At that time Dezong was indulging the frontier commands; hearing of Di's conduct, he could do nothing but assent.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was then indulging the military governors; hearing of Di's conduct, he could only acquiesce.

sentences.zh: 頔奏請無不從。

translations.literal: None of Di's memorial petitions went ungranted.
translations.idiomatic: Every petition Di submitted was granted.

sentences.zh: 於是公然聚斂，恣意虐殺，專以淩上威下為務。

translations.literal: Thereupon he openly amassed wealth, killed at will, and made it his business to bully superiors and intimidate subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He then openly extorted wealth, killed at will, and made bullying those above and terrorizing those below his specialty.

sentences.zh: 鄧州刺史元洪，頔誣以贓罪奏聞，朝旨不得已為流端州，命中使監焉。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong, Prefect of Deng Prefecture, was falsely accused by Di of embezzlement and reported; the court had no choice but to exile him to Duan Prefecture and ordered a palace envoy to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Di falsely accused Dengzhou prefect Yuan Hong of embezzlement; the court reluctantly exiled him to Duanzhou under escort by a palace envoy.

sentences.zh: 至隋州棗陽縣，頔命部將領士卒數百人，劫洪至襄州，拘留之。

translations.literal: When they reached Zaoyang county in Sui Prefecture, Di ordered a subordinate general to lead several hundred soldiers, seize Hong, and bring him to Xiang Prefecture, where he was detained.
translations.idiomatic: At Zaoyang in Suizhou, Di sent a subordinate with several hundred troops to abduct Hong to Xiangzhou and hold him there.

sentences.zh: 中使奔歸京師。

translations.literal: The palace envoy fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，笞之數十。

translations.literal: Dezong was angry and had him beaten several dozen strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was furious and had him flogged several dozen strokes.

sentences.zh: 頔又表洪其責太重，復降中使景忠信宣旨慰諭。

translations.literal: Di again memorialized that Hong's punishment was too severe; the court again sent the palace envoy Jing Zhongxin to proclaim an edict of consolation and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Di then memorialized that Hong's punishment was too harsh; the court sent palace envoy Jing Zhongxin with an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 遂除洪吉州長史，然後洪獲赴謫所。

translations.literal: Hong was then appointed Chief Clerk of Ji Prefecture, and only then was Hong able to reach his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was reassigned as chief clerk of Jizhou, and only then could he proceed to his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 又怒判官薛正倫，奏貶峽州長史。

translations.literal: He was again angry at his magistrate's aide Xue Zhenglun and memorialized to demote him to Chief Clerk of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Angry at his aide Xue Zhenglun, he memorialized to demote him to chief clerk of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 及敕下，頔怒已解，復奏請為判官，德宗皆從之。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived, Di's anger had already subsided; he again memorialized to have him as magistrate's aide, and Dezong granted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, Di's anger had passed; he petitioned to have Xue back as his aide, and Dezong agreed to everything.

sentences.zh: 正倫卒，未殯，頔以兵圍其宅，令孽男逼娶其嫡女。

translations.literal: When Zhenglun died, before the funeral Di surrounded his house with troops and ordered his illegitimate son to force marriage on his legitimate daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenglun died, before the funeral Di surrounded his house with troops and forced his illegitimate son to marry Zhenglun's legitimate daughter.

sentences.zh: 頔累遷至左僕射、平章事、燕國公。

translations.literal: Di was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councilor, and Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Di rose through the ranks to Left Vice Director, Grand Councilor, and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 俄而不奉詔旨，擅總兵據南陽，朝廷幾為之旰食。

translations.literal: Before long he did not obey imperial edicts, on his own authority gathered troops and held Nanyang; the court was nearly unable to eat until evening on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he defied imperial orders, mustered troops on his own authority, and seized Nanyang, leaving the court unable to eat for worry.

sentences.zh: 及憲宗即位，威肅四方，頔稍戒懼。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, his authority awed the four quarters, and Di became somewhat cautious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne, his authority awed the realm, and Di grew cautious.

sentences.zh: 以第四子季友求尚主。

translations.literal: He sought an imperial marriage for his fourth son Jiyou.
translations.idiomatic: He sought an imperial marriage for his fourth son, Jiyou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以長女永昌公主降焉。

translations.literal: Xianzong bestowed his eldest daughter, Princess Yongchang, in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong gave him his eldest daughter, Princess Yongchang, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 其第二子方，屢諷其父歸朝入覲，冊拜司空、平章事。

translations.literal: His second son Fang repeatedly urged his father to return to court and pay homage; he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Fang repeatedly urged him to return to court; Di was then appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 元和中，內官梁守謙掌樞密，頗招權利。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, the inner attendant Liang Shouqian controlled the Privy Council and greatly sought profit and power.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, eunuch Liang Shouqian controlled the Privy Council and amassed considerable power.

sentences.zh: 有梁正言者，勇於射利，自言與守謙宗盟情厚，頔子敏與之遊處。

translations.literal: There was one Liang Zhengyan, bold in pursuing profit, who claimed close clan ties with Shouqian; Di's son Min associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Liang Zhengyan, bold in pursuit of profit, claimed close ties with Shouqian; Di's son Min kept company with him.

sentences.zh: 正言取頔財賄，言賂守謙，以求出鎮。

translations.literal: Zhengyan took bribes from Di, saying he would bribe Shouqian to obtain a posting as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan took Di's money, promising to bribe Shouqian to secure an outside command for him.

sentences.zh: 久之無效，敏責其貨於正言。

translations.literal: After a long time with no result, Min demanded his goods back from Zhengyan.
translations.idiomatic: When nothing came of it, Min demanded his money back from Zhengyan.

sentences.zh: 乃誘正言之僮，支解棄於混中。

translations.literal: He then lured Zhengyan's slave boy, dismembered him, and cast the remains into the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: He then lured Zhengyan's slave boy, dismembered him, and dumped the body in the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 八年春，敏奴王再榮詣銀臺門告其事，即日捕頔孔目官沈璧、家僮十余人，於內侍獄鞫問。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, Min's slave Wang Zairong went to the Yintai Gate to report the matter; that same day more than ten of Di's clerks including Shen Bi and household slaves were arrested and interrogated in the Inner Attendants' Prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 813, Min's slave Wang Zairong reported the crime at the Yintai Gate; that day more than ten of Di's clerks, including Shen Bi, and household slaves were arrested and interrogated in the eunuchs' prison.

sentences.zh: 尋出付臺獄，詔御史中丞薛存誠、刑部侍郎王播、大理卿武少儀為三司使按問，乃搜死奴於其第，獲之。

translations.literal: Soon they were transferred to the Court Prison; the edict appointed Censor-in-Chief Xue Cuncheng, Vice Minister of Justice Wang Bo, and Grand Court Judge Wu Shaoyi as the Three Offices commissioners to investigate; they then searched for the murdered slave at his residence and found him.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon transferred to the Court Prison; Xue Cuncheng, Wang Bo, and Wu Shaoyi were appointed as the Three Offices commissioners to investigate, and the dismembered slave was found at Di's residence.

sentences.zh: 頔率其男贊善大夫正、駙馬都尉季友，素服單騎，將赴闕下，待罪於建福門。

translations.literal: Di led his sons—the Academician-Companion Zheng and the Imperial Son-in-Law Jiyou—in plain dress on a single horse, intending to go to the palace and await punishment at the Jianfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Di led his sons Zheng and Jiyou, the imperial son-in-law, in plain dress on horseback to the palace to await punishment at the Jianfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 門司不納，退於街南，負墻而立，遣人進表。

translations.literal: The gate officers would not admit them; they withdrew to the south of the street, stood with their backs to the wall, and sent someone to submit a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The gate officers refused them entry; they withdrew to the south side of the street, stood against the wall, and sent in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 閣門使以無引不受，日沒方歸。

translations.literal: The Gatekeeper Commissioner, on the grounds that there was no presentation credential, would not receive it; only at sunset did they return.
translations.idiomatic: The gate commissioner refused the memorial for lack of proper credentials; they did not return until sunset.

sentences.zh: 明日，復待罪於建福門。

translations.literal: The next day they again awaited punishment at the Jianfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they again waited for punishment at the Jianfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 宰相喻令還第，貶為恩王傅。

translations.literal: The chief ministers instructed them to return to their residence; he was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of En.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers told them to go home; Di was demoted to tutor of the Prince of En.

sentences.zh: 敏長流雷州，錮身發遣。

translations.literal: Min was exiled far to Lei Prefecture, sent off in shackles.
translations.idiomatic: Min was exiled to Leizhou in shackles.

sentences.zh: 殿中少監、駙馬都尉季友，追奪兩任官階，令其家循省。

translations.literal: Jiyou, Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Imperial Son-in-Law, had two ranks of office stripped posthumously [retroactively], and his household was ordered to reflect on their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou, Vice Director of the Palace Service and imperial son-in-law, had two ranks stripped and was ordered to reflect on his household's conduct.

sentences.zh: 左贊善大夫正、秘書丞方並停見任。

translations.literal: Zheng, Left Academician-Companion, and Fang, Secretary of the Secretariat, were both suspended from their current posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Fang were both suspended from their current posts.

sentences.zh: 孔目官沈璧決四十，配流封州。

translations.literal: The clerk Shen Bi was sentenced to forty strokes and exiled to Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Shen Bi was flogged forty strokes and exiled to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 奴犀牛與劉幹同手殺人，宜付京兆府決殺。

translations.literal: The slaves Xiniu and Liu Gan had jointly killed a man with their own hands; they should be handed to the Jingzhao Prefecture for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The slaves Xiniu and Liu Gan, who had jointly committed murder, were handed to the Jingzhao authorities for execution.

sentences.zh: 敏行至商山賜死。

translations.literal: When Min reached Shang Mountain he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Min was granted death by edict when he reached Shang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 梁正言、僧鑒虛並付京兆府決殺。

translations.literal: Liang Zhengyan and the monk Jianxu were both handed to the Jingzhao Prefecture for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhengyan and the monk Jianxu were both handed to the Jingzhao authorities for execution.

sentences.zh: 頔其年十月，改授太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Di was reassigned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That October Di was reassigned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年，王師討淮、蔡，諸侯貢財助軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the imperial army campaigned against Huai and Cai; the feudal lords presented wealth to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 815 the imperial army campaigned against Huai and Cai, and the regional lords sent funds to support the war effort.

sentences.zh: 頔進銀七千兩、金五百兩、玉帶二，詔不納，復還之。

translations.literal: Di presented seven thousand taels of silver, five hundred taels of gold, and two jade belts; an edict declined them and they were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Di offered seven thousand taels of silver, five hundred of gold, and two jade belts; the court declined them and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 十三年，頔表求致仕。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Di memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 818 Di petitioned to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 宰臣擬授太子少保，御筆改為太子賓客。

translations.literal: The chief ministers proposed appointing him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; the emperor's own brush changed it to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers proposed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; the emperor's own hand changed it to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年八月卒，贈太保，謚曰「厲」。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he died; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title "Li" (Harsh).
translations.idiomatic: He died that August and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Li, "Harsh."

sentences.zh: 其子季友從獵苑中，訴於穆宗，賜謚曰「思」。

translations.literal: His son Jiyou, while accompanying a hunt in the imperial park, appealed to Muzong, who granted the posthumous title "Si" (Reflective).
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiyou, while hunting in the imperial park, appealed to Emperor Muzong, who changed the posthumous name to Si, "Reflective."

sentences.zh: 右丞張正甫封敕，請還本謚。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhang Zhengfu sealed the edict and requested restoration of the original posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Zhang Zhengfu sealed the edict and petitioned to restore the original posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 右補闕高鉞上疏論之曰：

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Gao Tie submitted a memorial discussing it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Officer Gao Tie submitted a memorial arguing:

sentences.zh: 夫謚者，所以懲惡勸善，激濁揚清，使忠臣義士知勸，亂臣賊子知懼。

translations.literal: Posthumous titles exist to punish evil and encourage good, to stir the muddy and raise the clear, so that loyal ministers and righteous men know encouragement and rebellious ministers and wicked sons know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous names exist to punish the wicked and encourage the good, to lift the worthy and cast down the base, so loyal servants take heart and traitors take warning.

sentences.zh: 雖竊位於當時，死加惡謚者，所以懲暴戾，垂沮勸。

translations.literal: Even if one usurped position in one's own time, adding a harsh posthumous title at death is how to punish violence and arrogance and leave a warning behind.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who held power in life may receive harsh posthumous names at death, to punish cruelty and leave a lasting warning.

sentences.zh: 孔子修《春秋》，亂臣賊子懼，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: When Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers and wicked sons were fearful—surely it was for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, traitors feared judgment—that is precisely the point.

sentences.zh: 垂範如此而不能救，況又隳其典法乎？

translations.literal: When the model set forth is such and yet cannot save us, how much less if we also destroy its canonical law?
translations.idiomatic: If even such a precedent cannot restrain us, what will become of the law when we overturn it outright?

sentences.zh: 臣風聞此事是徐泗節度使李愬奏請。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard on good authority that this matter was memorialized by Li Su, Military Governor of Xu-Si.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that this change was requested by Li Su, military governor of Xu and Si.

sentences.zh: 李愬勛臣節將，陛下寵其勛勞，賜其爵祿、車服、第宅則可，若亂朝廷典法，將何以沮勸？

translations.literal: Li Su is a meritorious frontier commander; Your Majesty may favor his achievements and grant him rank, salary, carriages, robes, and mansions—but if he disrupts the court's canonical law, how will encouragement and warning be preserved?
translations.idiomatic: Li Su is a meritorious commander; Your Majesty may reward his service with rank, salary, carriages, robes, and estates—but if he is allowed to overturn court precedent, how will reward and warning retain any force?

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「唯名與器，不可以假人。」

translations.literal: Zhongni said: "Titles and regalia alone may not be lent to others."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Titles and regalia must not be lent to others."

sentences.zh: 名器，君之所司，若以假人，與之政也，政亡則國家從之。

translations.literal: Titles and regalia are what the ruler controls; if lent to others, it is giving them government; when government perishes, the state follows after.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and regalia are the sovereign's to dispense; to lend them to others is to yield power—and when power is lost, the state follows.

sentences.zh: 頔頃鎮襄、漢，殺戮不辜，恣行兇暴。

translations.literal: Di lately governed Xiang and Han, slaughtered the innocent, and indulged in violence and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Di lately governed Xiang and Han, slaughtered the innocent, and indulged in open brutality.

sentences.zh: 移軍襄、鄧，迫脅朝廷，擅留逐臣，僥遮天使。

translations.literal: He shifted troops between Xiang and Deng, coerced the court, on his own authority detained an exiled official, and presumptuously obstructed the imperial envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He moved troops between Xiang and Deng, intimidated the court, detained an exiled official on his own authority, and brazenly obstructed an imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 當先朝嗣位之始，貴安反側，以靖四方。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the previous reign's succession, the court valued pacifying the restless to settle the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the previous reign, the court prized pacifying unrest to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 幸免鈇鉞之誅，得全腰領而斃，誠宜謚之「繆厲」，以沮兇邪，豈可曲加美名，以惠奸宄。

translations.literal: He narrowly escaped execution by axe and halberd, kept his neck whole and died a natural death—he truly ought to be given the posthumous title "Miu Li" (Erring and Harsh) to deter the vicious and evil; how can a flattering fine name be bent to benefit traitors and villains?
translations.idiomatic: He narrowly escaped execution, died with his neck intact, and ought to receive the posthumous name "Miu Li" to deter the wicked—how can a flattering name be granted to reward a villain?

sentences.zh: 如此，則是於頔生為奸臣，死獲美謚，竊恐天下有識之士，謂聖朝無人，有此倒置。

translations.literal: If so, then Yu Di was a treacherous minister in life yet obtained a fine posthumous title in death; your subject fears that men of discernment throughout the realm will say the sagely dynasty has no one [to uphold standards], with such an inversion.
translations.idiomatic: If so, Di was a traitor in life yet receives a flattering name in death; I fear discerning men everywhere will conclude that the court has no one left to uphold standards.

sentences.zh: 伏請速追前詔，卻依太常謚為厲，使朝典無虧，國章不濫。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly requests that the previous edict be quickly revoked and that the Court of Rites' posthumous title Li be restored, so that court precedent suffers no loss and national regulations are not debased.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to revoke the recent edict and restore the Court of Rites' posthumous name Li, so court precedent remains intact and state honor is not debased.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王彥威又疏曰：

translations.literal: Court of Rites Academician Wang Yanwei also submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Court of Rites academician Wang Yanwei also submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王立謚法者，所以彰善惡、垂勸誡。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity established the law of posthumous titles in order to display good and evil and leave encouragement and warning behind.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity established posthumous naming to distinguish good from evil and leave lasting lessons behind.

sentences.zh: 使一字之褒，賞逾紱冕；

translations.literal: so that a single word of praise was reward surpassing robes and caps;
translations.idiomatic: So that a single word of praise outweighed robes and caps in reward;

sentences.zh: 一言之貶，辱過朝市。

translations.literal: a single word of censure was disgrace surpassing the court and market.
translations.idiomatic: and a single word of censure brought disgrace worse than public shame in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 此有國之典禮，陛下勸懲之大柄也。

translations.literal: This is the canonical ritual of a state; it is Your Majesty's great handle for encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: This is a state's canonical ritual and Your Majesty's chief instrument of reward and warning.

sentences.zh: 頔頃擁節旄，肆行暴虐，人神共憤，法令不容。

translations.literal: Di lately held the commander's banner and flag, indulged in violence and cruelty; men and spirits alike were enraged, and the law could not tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Di lately held military command and indulged in open brutality until men and spirits alike were outraged and the law could no longer tolerate him.

sentences.zh: 擅興全師，僭為正樂，侵辱中使，擅止制囚，殺戮不辜，誅求無度，臣故定謚為厲。

translations.literal: He on his own authority mobilized full armies, presumptuously performed orthodox music, insulted palace envoys, on his own authority halted imperial prisoners, slaughtered the innocent, and extorted without limit—your subject therefore fixed his posthumous title as Li.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized whole armies on his own authority, presumptuously performed state music, insulted palace envoys, detained imperial prisoners, slaughtered the innocent, and extorted without limit—I therefore fixed his posthumous name as Li.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不忍，改賜為「思」，誠出聖慈，實害聖政。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty could not bear it and changed the grant to "Si"; it truly sprang from sagely compassion, but in fact it harms sagely governance.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty, moved by compassion, has changed it to "Si"—a kindness in intent, but a harm to governance in fact.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下自臨宸扆，懋建大中，聞善若驚，從諫不倦。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that since Your Majesty ascended the imperial throne, you have vigorously established the Great Central reign, startled at hearing good, and never weary of following remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, you have vigorously pursued the Great Central ideal, welcomed good counsel eagerly, and never wearied of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 況當統天立極之始，所謂執法慎名之時，一垂恩光，大啟僥幸。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of uniting Heaven and establishing the pole—the time called for enforcing law and guarding names—a single bestowal of favor greatly opens the door to presumption.
translations.idiomatic: At the very start of your reign—the time when law and honor must be guarded most strictly—a single act of mercy opens wide the door to presumption.

sentences.zh: 且如頔之不法，然而陛下不忍加懲，臣恐今後不逞之徒如頔者眾矣！

translations.literal: Moreover, for one as lawless as Di, yet Your Majesty could not bear to punish him—your subject fears that hereafter unruly men like Di will be many!
translations.idiomatic: If one as lawless as Di goes unpunished because Your Majesty cannot bear it, I fear many more like him will follow!

sentences.zh: 死援頔例，陛下何以處之？

translations.literal: When the dead cite Di's precedent, how will Your Majesty deal with them?
translations.idiomatic: When the dead cite Di's precedent, how will Your Majesty answer them?

sentences.zh: 是恩曲於前而弊生於後。

translations.literal: This is favor bent in the present while harm arises afterward.
translations.idiomatic: This bends mercy in the present only to breed harm afterward.

sentences.zh: 若以李吉甫有賜謚之例，則甫之為相也，有犯上殺人之罪乎？

translations.literal: If one cites Li Jifu as having a precedent of granted posthumous title, when Jifu was chief minister, did he have the crime of offending superiors and killing men?
translations.idiomatic: If one cites Li Jifu's precedent of a granted posthumous name, did Jifu as chief minister ever commit crimes of treason and murder?

sentences.zh: 以頔況之，恐非倫類。

translations.literal: Comparing Di to him, I fear they are not of the same category.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Di, I fear they are not in the same category at all.

sentences.zh: 如以頔常入財助國，改過來覲，兩使絕域，可以贖論，夫傷物害人，剝下奉上，納賄求幸，尤不可長其漸焉。

translations.literal: If because Di often presented wealth to assist the state, reformed his faults and came to court, and twice served as envoy to distant regions, one may argue for redemption—yet harming things and harming men, stripping the lower ranks to serve the upper, and offering bribes to seek favor especially must not be allowed to grow by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If Di's occasional gifts to the state, his belated court appearance, and his service as envoy to distant lands are held to redeem him, consider still that harming the people, stripping the poor to enrich the throne, and buying favor with bribes must never be encouraged to spread.

sentences.zh: 自兩河宿兵，垂七十年，王師憓征，瘡磐未息。

translations.literal: Since troops were stationed in the two He [regions], nearly seventy years have passed; the imperial army has campaigned repeatedly, yet wounds and ruins have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly seventy years troops had been stationed in the two He regions; imperial campaigns came one after another, yet the wounds of war had not healed.

sentences.zh: 及張茂昭以易定入覲，程權以滄景歸朝，故恩禮殊尤，以勸來者。

translations.literal: When Zhang Maozhao came to court from Yi and Ding, and Cheng Quan returned to the dynasty from Cang and Jing, therefore favor and ritual were exceptionally generous to encourage those who would come after.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Maozhao came to court from Yi and Ding and Cheng Quan returned from Cang and Jing, the court lavished exceptional honors to encourage others to follow.

sentences.zh: 而於頔以文吏之職，居腹心之地，而倔強犯命，不獲已而入朝，豈茂昭之比乎！

translations.literal: Yet Yu Di, in a civil official's post, occupied the heartland region, yet was stubborn and defied orders, coming to court only when he had no choice—how can he be compared to Maozhao!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Di, a civil official holding a post in the empire's heartland, had defied the throne and come to court only under compulsion—how can he be compared to Maozhao!

sentences.zh: 縱有入財使遠之勤，何以掩其惡跡！

translations.literal: Even if he had the merit of presenting wealth and serving as envoy to distant lands, how could that cover his evil tracks!
translations.idiomatic: Even if his gifts and embassies to distant lands counted as merit, how could they cover his crimes!

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下恩由義斷，澤以禮成，褒貶道存，僥幸路絕，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will let favor be decided by righteousness and grace be completed by ritual, so that the way of praise and blame endures and the path of presumption is cut off—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to let mercy follow righteousness and favor be bounded by ritual, so praise and blame retain their force and presumption finds no path—the realm would be greatly fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不報，竟謚為思。

translations.literal: The memorials received no response; in the end the posthumous title was fixed as Si.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials went unanswered; in the end the posthumous name Si stood.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，以戚裏勛家諸貴引用於方，復至和王傅，家富於財。

translations.literal: In the Changqing era, through the recommendation of noble families related by marriage to the imperial clan, Fang was again made Tutor of the Prince of He; his household was rich in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing reign, connections among the imperial in-laws brought Fang back as tutor of the Prince of He; his household was very wealthy.

sentences.zh: 方交結遊俠，務於速進。

translations.literal: Fang associated with roaming knights-errant and strove for rapid advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Fang cultivated ties with wandering swordsmen and pressed for rapid advancement.

sentences.zh: 元稹作相，欲以其策平河朔群盜，方以策畫幹稹。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen became chief minister, he wished to use Fang's stratagems to pacify the bandit groups of Hebei; Fang presented his plans to win over Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen became chief minister, he hoped to use Fang's plans to pacify the Hebei bandits; Fang pressed his schemes upon Zhen.

sentences.zh: 而李逢吉之黨欲傾裴度，乃令人告稹欲結客刺度。

translations.literal: But the faction of Li Fengji wished to topple Pei Du and had someone report that Zhen intended to recruit clients to assassinate Du.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Fengji's faction, seeking to destroy Pei Du, had someone accuse Zhen of plotting to hire assassins against Du.

sentences.zh: 事下法司，按鞫無狀，而方竟坐誅。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the judicial offices; investigation found no basis, yet Fang in the end was executed on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the courts; investigation found no proof, yet Fang was executed nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 韓弘，潁川人。

translations.literal: Han Hong was a native of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong came from Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 其祖、父無聞，世居滑之匡城。

translations.literal: His grandfather and father are not recorded; the family had long resided at Kuangcheng in Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is recorded of his grandfather and father; the family had long lived at Kuangcheng in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，依母族。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he relied on his mother's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his mother's family.

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐即其舅也。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanzuo was his maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo was his uncle on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 事玄佐為州掾，累奏試大理評事。

translations.literal: He served Xuanzuo as a prefectural aide and was repeatedly memorialized for trial appointment as Grand Court Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xuanzuo as a prefectural aide and was repeatedly nominated for trial appointment as Grand Court Assessor.

sentences.zh: 玄佐卒，子士寧被逐。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo died, his son Shinning was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzuo died, his son Shinning was driven from office.

sentences.zh: 弘出汴州，為宋州南城將。

translations.literal: Hong left Bian Prefecture and became Southern City Commander of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hong left Bianzhou and became commander of the southern garrison at Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉全諒時為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Quanliang was Director of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Quanliang was director of military affairs at Bian.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，全諒卒，汴軍懷玄佐之惠，又以弘長厚，共請為留後，環監軍使請表其事，朝廷亦以玄佐故許之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, Quanliang died; the Bian army remembered Xuanzuo's kindness, and because Hong was also generous and steady, they jointly requested him as acting military governor; Huan, the army supervisor, requested a memorial on the matter, and the court also granted it for Xuanzuo's sake.
translations.idiomatic: In 799 Quanliang died; the Bian troops, remembering Xuanzuo's kindness and finding Hong steady and generous, asked that he be made acting military governor; supervisor Huan memorialized the court, which approved the request out of regard for Xuanzuo.

sentences.zh: 自試大理評事檢校工部尚書、汴州刺史，兼御史大夫、宣武軍節度副大使知節度事、宋亳汴潁觀察等使。

translations.literal: From trial Grand Court Assessor he was made Acting Minister of Works, Prefect of Bian, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Vice Military Governor of the Xuanwu Army with authority over military governorship affairs, and Surveillance Commissioner of Song, Bo, Bian, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: From trial Grand Court Assessor he rose to Acting Minister of Works and prefect of Bian, also serving as censor-in-chief, vice military governor of the Xuanwu army with full command authority, and surveillance commissioner of Song, Bo, Bian, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 時吳少誠遣人至汴，密與劉全諒謀，因曲環卒襲陳許。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shao-cheng sent men to Bian to plot secretly with Liu Quanliang to take advantage of Qu Huan's death and raid Chen and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng then sent agents to Bian to plot secretly with Quanliang for a raid on Chen and Xu when Qu Huan died.

sentences.zh: 會全諒卒，其人在傳舍，弘喜獲節鉞，即斬其人以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that Quanliang died; the men were at the relay station; Hong, delighted to have obtained the commander's seal and staff, immediately beheaded them and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanliang died just then; the plotters were at the relay station; Hong, delighted to secure command, beheaded them at once and reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 立出軍三千，助禁軍共討少誠。

translations.literal: He immediately sent out three thousand troops to assist the imperial guard in jointly campaigning against Shao-cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dispatched three thousand troops to join the imperial guard in campaigning against Shaocheng.

sentences.zh: 汴州自劉士寧之後，軍益驕恣，及陸長源遇害，頗輕主帥。

translations.literal: Since Liu Shinning, the Bian army had grown ever more arrogant and insubordinate; after Lu Changyuan was murdered, they quite looked down on their commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Shinning's time the Bian troops had grown ever more arrogant; after Lu Changyuan was murdered, they openly despised their commanders.

sentences.zh: 其為亂魁黨數十百人。

translations.literal: Those who were ringleaders of disorder numbered several tens to a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen to a hundred men led the disorder.

sentences.zh: 弘視事數月，皆知其人。

translations.literal: After Hong had taken office several months, he knew them all.
translations.idiomatic: Within months of taking office, Hong knew them all by name.

sentences.zh: 有部將劉鍔者，兇卒之魁也。

translations.literal: There was a subordinate general, Liu E, who was the chief of the violent soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: One subordinate, Liu E, was chief among the violent troops.

sentences.zh: 弘欲大振威望。

translations.literal: Hong wished to greatly revive his authority and prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Hong wished to restore his authority decisively.

sentences.zh: 一日，引短兵於衙門，召鍔與其黨三百，數其罪，盡斬之以徇，血流道中。

translations.literal: One day he led short weapons [infantry] at the yamen gate, summoned E and his faction of three hundred, enumerated their crimes, and beheaded them all to display; blood flowed in the roadway.
translations.idiomatic: One day he posted guards at the yamen gate, summoned E and his three hundred followers, recited their crimes, and executed them all in public; blood ran in the street.

sentences.zh: 弘對賓僚言笑自若。

translations.literal: Hong conversed and laughed with his guests and staff as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Hong chatted and laughed with his staff as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 自是訖弘入朝，二十余年，軍眾十萬，無敢怙亂者。

translations.literal: From then until Hong came to court, more than twenty years, with an army of one hundred thousand, none dared rely on disorder.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years thereafter, until Hong came to court, none among his hundred thousand troops dared stir disorder again.

sentences.zh: 累授檢校左右僕射、司空。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Acting Left and Right Vice Director and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to acting vice director and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, he was made Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne, Hong was made associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時王鍔檢校司空、平章事。

translations.literal: At that time Wang E was Acting Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang E held the posts of acting Minister of Works and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 致書於宰臣武元衡，恥在王鍔之下。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng, ashamed to rank below Wang E.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to chief minister Wu Yuanheng, protesting that he should not rank below Wang E.

sentences.zh: 憲宗方欲用形勢以臨淮西，乃授以司徒、平章事，班在鍔上。

translations.literal: Xianzong was then wishing to use strategic pressure against Huai West and therefore appointed him Minister of Education and Grand Councilor, ranking above E.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, preparing to bring pressure on Huai West, appointed him Minister of Education and grand councilor, ranking above Wang E.

sentences.zh: 及用嚴綬為招討，為賊所敗，弘方鎮汴州，當兩河賊之沖要，朝廷慮其異志，欲以兵柄授之，而令李光顏、烏重胤實當旗鼓。

translations.literal: When Yan Shou was used as campaign commander and was defeated by the rebels, Hong was then governing Bian Prefecture at the strategic choke point of the two He bandits; the court feared his divergent intentions, wished to grant him the military command, yet had Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin actually bear the banners and drums.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shou was appointed campaign commander and defeated, Hong still held Bianzhou at the strategic junction of the Hebei rebels; the court feared disloyalty and wished to give him nominal command while Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin led the actual fighting.

sentences.zh: 乃授弘淮西諸軍行營都統，令兵部郎中、知制誥李程宣賜官告。

translations.literal: Hong was then appointed Overall Commander of the Huai West campaign armies; Director Li Cheng of the Ministry of War, who also drafted edicts, was ordered to proclaim and bestow the commission document.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was appointed overall commander of the Huai West campaign armies, and Li Cheng of the Ministry of War was sent to deliver the commission.

sentences.zh: 弘實不離理所，唯令其子公武率師三千隸李光顏軍。

translations.literal: Hong in fact did not leave his headquarters; he only ordered his son Gongwu to lead three thousand troops subordinate to Li Guangyan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Hong in fact never left his headquarters, sending only his son Gongwu with three thousand men to serve under Li Guangyan.

sentences.zh: 弘雖居統帥，常不欲諸軍立功，陰為逗撓之計。

translations.literal: Although Hong held the post of overall commander, he often did not wish the armies to achieve merit and secretly made plans to delay and obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: Though nominal commander, Hong often did not want the armies to win victories and secretly worked to delay and obstruct them.

sentences.zh: 每聞獻捷，輒數日不怡，其危國邀功如是。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard of victories reported, he would be displeased for several days; such was his endangering the state to seek merit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever news of victory arrived, he was displeased for days—such was his willingness to endanger the state for his own advantage.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟誅，以統帥功，加檢校司徒、兼侍中，封許國公，罷行營都統。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji was executed, for his merit as overall commander he was made Acting Minister of Education, concurrently Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Xu, and relieved of the campaign command.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji was executed, Hong was promoted to acting Minister of Education and palace attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Xu, and relieved of campaign command.

sentences.zh: 十四年，誅李師道，收復河南二州，弘大懼。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Li Shidao was executed and the two Henan prefectures were recovered; Hong was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In 819 Li Shidao was executed and two Henan prefectures recovered; Hong was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，盡攜汴之牙校千餘人入覲。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he brought more than a thousand Bian staff officers to court.
translations.idiomatic: That July he brought more than a thousand Bian staff officers to court.

sentences.zh: 對於便殿，拜舞之際，以其足疾，命中使掖之。

translations.literal: He was received in the informal hall; during bowing and dancing, because of his foot ailment, the emperor ordered a palace envoy to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Received in the informal hall, he was supported by a palace envoy during his bow because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 宴賜加等，預冊徽號大禮。

translations.literal: Banquets and gifts were of a higher grade; he participated in the great ceremony of proclaiming the honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: He received banquets and gifts of the highest grade and took part in the ceremony proclaiming the emperor's honorific title.

sentences.zh: 進絹三十五萬匹、騑三萬匹、銀器二百七十件。

translations.literal: He presented three hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand horses, and two hundred seventy pieces of silverware.
translations.idiomatic: He presented 350,000 bolts of silk, 30,000 horses, and 270 pieces of silverware.

sentences.zh: 三上章堅辭戎務，願留京師奉朝請。

translations.literal: Three times he submitted memorials firmly declining military affairs, wishing to remain in the capital to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he memorialized to resign military duties and remain in the capital as a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict read:

sentences.zh: 納大忠，樹嘉績，為臣所以明極節；

translations.literal: Receiving great loyalty and establishing fine achievements—this is how a minister manifests utmost integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Receiving great loyalty and establishing fine achievements—this is how a minister shows utmost integrity;

sentences.zh: 錫殊寵，進高秩，有國所以待元臣。

translations.literal: bestowing special favor and advancing to high rank—this is how a state treats its foremost ministers.
translations.idiomatic: bestowing special favor and advancing to high rank—this is how a state honors its foremost ministers.

sentences.zh: 況乎邦教誕敷，王言總會，百辟攸憲，四方式瞻。

translations.literal: Moreover, when state instruction is broadly spread and royal words are gathered together, the hundred officials take it as their model and the four quarters look up in hope.
translations.idiomatic: When state teaching spreads abroad and royal words gather the court, the hundred officials take their model from it and the four quarters look on in hope.

sentences.zh: 永念於懷，久虛其位，載揚成命，僉曰休哉。

translations.literal: Ever kept in mind, long vacant its post—now proclaiming the completed mandate, all say it is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Long kept in mind, long vacant—now the completed appointment is proclaimed, and all say it is excellent.

sentences.zh: 宣武軍節度副大使知節度事、汴宋亳潁等州觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司、守司徒、兼侍中、使持節汴州諸軍事、汴州刺史、上柱國、許國公、食邑三千戶韓弘，降神挺材，積厚成器；

translations.literal: Han Hong, Vice Military Governor of the Xuanwu Army with authority over military governorship affairs, Surveillance and Disposition Commissioner of Bian, Song, Bo, and Ying, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Three Excellencies, Acting Minister of Education, concurrently Palace Attendant, Commissioner with Staff for Bian Military Affairs, Prefect of Bian, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Xu with a fief of three thousand households—descended spirit, outstanding talent, accumulated depth becoming vessel;
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong, vice military governor of the Xuanwu army with full command authority, surveillance commissioner of Bian, Song, Bo, and Ying, Grand Master of the Court, acting Minister of Education and palace attendant, commissioner for Bian military affairs, prefect of Bian, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Xu with a fief of three thousand households—heaven-sent talent, long cultivation made whole;

sentences.zh: 中蘊深閎之量，外標嚴重之姿。

translations.literal: Within he harbored deep and vast capacity; outwardly he displayed stern and weighty bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Within he held deep and vast capacity; outwardly he bore stern and weighty dignity.

sentences.zh: 有匡國濟時之心，推誠不耀；

translations.literal: He had a heart to rectify the state and aid the age, sincere without display;
translations.idiomatic: He had a heart to save the state and aid the age, sincere without display;

sentences.zh: 有夷兇禁暴之略，仗義益彰。

translations.literal: he had stratagems to pacify the vicious and restrain violence, upholding righteousness ever more clearly.
translations.idiomatic: he had stratagems to pacify the vicious and restrain violence, and his righteousness shone all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 自鎮浚郊，二十余載，師徒稟訓而鹹肅，吏士奉法而愈明。

translations.literal: Since governing the Jun metropolitan region more than twenty years, troops received instruction and all were orderly; officials and clerks upheld law and grew ever clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the Bian region for more than twenty years, his troops were trained into discipline and his officials grew ever more law-abiding.

sentences.zh: 俗臻和平，人用庶富，威聲之重，隱若山崇。

translations.literal: Custom reached peace; the people grew prosperous; the weight of his prestige was hidden like a mountain's height.
translations.idiomatic: Peace prevailed, the people prospered, and his prestige loomed like a mountain.

sentences.zh: 屬者，淮濆濯征，命統群帥，克殄殘孽，惟乃有指蹤之功。

translations.literal: Recently, when the Huai banks were washed by campaign, he was ordered to command the group of commanders, exterminated the remnant rebels—only he had the merit of directing the pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the Huai region was swept by war, he was ordered to command the allied generals and helped exterminate the rebels—his merit lay in directing the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及齊境興妖，分師進討，遂梟元惡，惟乃有略地之效。

translations.literal: When the Qi borderlands raised rebellion and divided armies advanced to attack, the chief villain was beheaded—only he had the effect of seizing territory.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion rose on the Qi border and armies advanced, the chief villain was beheaded—his merit lay in securing territory.

sentences.zh: 既聞旋旆，俄請執珪，深陳魏闕之誠，遠繼韓侯之誌。

translations.literal: Having heard of the returning banners, he soon requested to present his jade tablet, deeply stating his sincerity toward the imperial court, distantly following the ambition of Marquis Han.
translations.idiomatic: When victory banners returned, he soon asked to present his jade tablet, declaring his loyalty to the throne and following the example of Marquis Han of old.

sentences.zh: 朝天有慶，就日方伸。

translations.literal: Facing Heaven there is celebration; approaching the sun his purpose extends.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court in celebration; his purpose found its day.

sentences.zh: 又抗表章，固辭戎旅，三加敦諭，所守彌堅。

translations.literal: Again he submitted memorials firmly declining military service; three times earnest instruction was added, yet what he upheld grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Again he memorialized to resign military duties; three times the court urged him on, yet he held all the firmer to his request.

sentences.zh: 於蕃於宣，諒切於註意；

translations.literal: In Fan and in Xuan, truly earnest in attention;
translations.idiomatic: In Fan and in Xuan, truly earnest in his attention;

sentences.zh: 我弼我輔，難違其衷懇。

translations.literal: my assistant, my support—it is hard to go against his heartfelt plea.
translations.idiomatic: my assistant and support—it is hard to refuse his heartfelt plea.

sentences.zh: 式遂良願，載兼上司。

translations.literal: Thus his good wish is fulfilled; he is also given charge of the chief ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his wish is granted; he is also given charge of the chief ministry.

sentences.zh: 論道之榮，因之以齊八政；

translations.literal: the glory of discussing the Way, thereby to align the eight policies;
translations.idiomatic: The glory of discussing the Way, thereby to align the eight policies of state;

sentences.zh: 中樞之長，升之以贊萬務。

translations.literal: head of the central pivot, elevated to assist in the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: head of the central pivot, elevated to assist in the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 玄袞赤舄，備於寵光；

translations.literal: dark robes and red shoes, complete in favor and glory;
translations.idiomatic: Dark robes and red shoes, complete in favor and glory;

sentences.zh: 不有其人，孰膺斯任？

translations.literal: Without such a man, who could undertake this charge?
translations.idiomatic: Without such a man, who could undertake this charge?

sentences.zh: 可守司徒、兼中書令。

translations.literal: He may hold the post of Minister of Education and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Minister of Education and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乃以吏部尚書張弘靖兼平章事，代弘鎮宣武。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Personnel Zhang Hongjing was made Associate Grand Councilor to replace Hong in governing Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhang Hongjing was made associate grand councilor to replace Hong as military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩，以弘攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When Xianzong died, Hong was made acting Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong died, Hong served as acting grand minister.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，以本官兼河中尹、河中晉絳節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, with his existing offices he was also made Prefect of Hezhong, Military Governor and Surveillance Commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 820, while retaining his existing posts, he was also made prefect of Hezhong and military governor of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 時弘弟充為鄭滑節度使，子公武為鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: At that time Hong's younger brother Chong was Military Governor of Zheng and Hua, and his son Gongwu was Military Governor of Fu and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hong's brother Chong was military governor of Zheng and Hua, and his son Gongwu was military governor of Fu and Fang.

sentences.zh: 父子兄弟，皆秉節鉞，人臣之寵，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: Father, sons, and brothers all held the commander's seal and staff; the favor shown a subject reached its peak in that age.
translations.idiomatic: Father, sons, and brothers all held military commands—the favor shown a subject had no parallel in that age.

sentences.zh: 二年，請老乞罷戎鎮，三表從之。

translations.literal: In the second year he requested old age leave and begged to relinquish military governorship; three memorials were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he petitioned three times to retire from military command; the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 依前守司徒、中書令。

translations.literal: As before he held Minister of Education and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his posts as Minister of Education and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月病卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he died of illness, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness that December, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，賻絹二千匹、布七百端、米粟千碩。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant; funeral gifts were two thousand bolts of silk, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and a thousand dan of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant; funeral gifts included two thousand bolts of silk, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and a thousand dan of grain.

sentences.zh: 初，弘鎮大梁二十餘載，四州征賦皆為己有，未嘗上供。

translations.literal: At first, Hong governed Great Liang more than twenty years; the tax levies of the four prefectures were all kept for himself and never submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years Hong governed Bian; the tax revenues of four prefectures were kept for himself and never sent to the court.

sentences.zh: 有私錢百萬貫、粟三百萬斛、馬七千匹，兵械稱是。

translations.literal: He had private cash of a million strings, grain of three million hu, seven thousand horses, and military equipment to match.
translations.idiomatic: He held private cash of a million strings, three million hu of grain, seven thousand horses, and military equipment to match.

sentences.zh: 專務聚財積粟，峻法樹威。

translations.literal: He devoted himself solely to amassing wealth and hoarding grain, using harsh law to establish authority.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to amassing wealth and grain and used harsh law to establish his authority.

sentences.zh: 而莊重寡言，沈謀勇斷，鄰封如吳少誠、李師道輩皆憚之。

translations.literal: Yet he was grave and sparing of words, deep in counsel and bold in decision; neighboring commands such as Wu Shao-cheng and Li Shidao all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was grave and sparing of words, deep in counsel and bold in decision; neighbors such as Wu Shaocheng and Li Shidao all feared him.

sentences.zh: 詔使宣諭，弘多倨待。

translations.literal: When edict envoys came to proclaim instructions, Hong often treated them arrogantly.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial envoys came with edicts, Hong often treated them arrogantly.

sentences.zh: 及齊、蔡賊平，勢屈入覲，兩朝寵待加等，弘竟以名位始終，人臣之幸也。

translations.literal: When the Qi and Cai rebels were pacified, his power bent and he came to court; both reigns treated him with added favor, and Hong in the end kept rank and title to the end—the fortune of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi and Cai rebels were pacified, his power broken, he came to court; both reigns lavished favor on him, and Hong kept rank and title to the end—the rare fortune of a subject.

sentences.zh: 時公武已卒，弘孫紹宗嗣。

translations.literal: At that time Gongwu had already died; Hong's grandson Shaozong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Gongwu had already died; Hong's grandson Shaozong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 公武自宣武馬步都虞候將兵誅蔡，賊平，檢校右散騎常侍、鄜州刺史、鄜坊等州節度使。

translations.literal: Gongwu, from Xuanwu Cavalry and Infantry Director, led troops to execute Cai; when the rebels were pacified, he was made Acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prefect of Fu, and Military Governor of Fu and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongwu, as Xuanwu cavalry and infantry director, led troops against Cai; when the rebels were pacified, he was made acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, prefect of Fu, and military governor of Fu and Fang.

sentences.zh: 丁所生憂，起復金吾將軍，仍舊職。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his biological mother, was recalled from mourning as Golden Guard General, and retained his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his birth mother, he was recalled from mourning as Golden Guard General and retained his former post.

sentences.zh: 十四年，父弘入朝，公武乞罷節度，入為右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when his father Hong came to court, Gongwu begged to relinquish military governorship and entered office as Right Golden Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In 819, when his father Hong came to court, Gongwu asked to resign his command and entered office as Right Golden Guard General.

sentences.zh: 既而弘出鎮河中，季父充移鎮宣武，公武嘆曰：「二父聯居重鎮，吾以孺子當執金吾職，家門之盛，懼不克勝。」

translations.literal: Soon after Hong went out to govern Hezhong and his younger uncle Chong was transferred to govern Xuanwu, Gongwu sighed and said: "Two fathers jointly hold great commands; I, a mere youth, am to hold the Golden Guard post—the family's glory, I fear I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: When Hong took command at Hezhong and his uncle Chong at Xuanwu, Gongwu sighed: "Two elders hold great commands while I, a mere youth, hold the Golden Guard post—the family's glory may be more than I can bear."

sentences.zh: 堅辭宿衛，改右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined palace guard duty and was changed to Right Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined palace guard duty and was reassigned as Right Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 性頗恭遜，不以富貴自處。

translations.literal: His nature was quite respectful and modest; he did not comport himself by wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was respectful and modest and did not comport himself as one of great wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 弘罷河中，居崇裏第；

translations.literal: When Hong relinquished Hezhong, he resided at a mansion in Chong Lane;
translations.idiomatic: When Hong left Hezhong, he lived in a mansion on Chong Lane;

sentences.zh: 公武居宣陽裏之北門，因省父，無疾暴卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Gongwu lived at the north gate of Xuanyang Lane; while visiting his father he suddenly died without illness and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Gongwu lived at the north gate of Xuanyang Lane; while visiting his father he died suddenly without prior illness and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 充依舅劉玄佐，歷河陽、昭義牙將。

translations.literal: Chong relied on his uncle Liu Xuanzuo and successively served as a garrison officer at Heyang and Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong relied on his uncle Liu Xuanzuo and served as a garrison officer at Heyang and Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 及兄弘節制宣武，召歸主親兵，奏授御史大夫。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Hong governed Xuanwu, he was recalled to command the personal troops and memorialized for appointment as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Hong governed Xuanwu, he was recalled to command the personal guard and memorialized for appointment as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 弘頗酷法，人人不自保。

translations.literal: Hong was quite harsh in law; every man could not preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's rule was harsh, and no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 充獨謙恭執禮，未嘗懈怠，由是遍得士心。

translations.literal: Chong alone was humble and respectful in observing ritual; he never slackened; thereby he everywhere won the hearts of the men.
translations.idiomatic: Chong alone remained humble and courteous, never slackening in duty, and thus won the loyalty of the troops throughout the command.

sentences.zh: 然以親逼權重，常不自安。

translations.literal: Yet because as a close relative he pressed upon great authority, he was often not at ease himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a close kinsman wielding great authority, he often felt uneasy in his position.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，因獵近郊，單騎歸於洛陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, taking advantage of a hunt in the near suburbs, he returned alone on horseback to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe (811), while hunting near the suburbs, he rode alone back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方姑息弘，亦憐充之無異志，擢拜右金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the court was still indulging Hong, and also took pity on Chong's having no divergent ambition; he was promoted and appointed General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The court was still conciliating Hong and, believing Chong had no designs of his own, promoted him to general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 十二月，轉大將軍，歷少府監。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to grand general, and successively served as Director of the Palace Stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was made grand general and subsequently served as director of the palace stores.

sentences.zh: 十五年，代侄公武為鄜坊節度使、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he replaced his nephew Gongwu as military governor of Fufang and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (820) he replaced his nephew Gongwu as military governor of Fufang, with the acting title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，幽、鎮、魏復亂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, You, Zhen, and Wei again fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing (822), the You, Zhen, and Wei regions rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以王承元有冀卒數千在滑州，恐封疆相接，復相勸誘。

translations.literal: The court, because Wang Chengyuan had several thousand Ji troops at Hua Prefecture, feared that as their territories adjoined they might again mutually persuade and entice one another.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyuan still had several thousand Hebei troops at Hua Prefecture; fearing the adjacent commands might incite one another again, the court sought to rearrange them.

sentences.zh: 命充與承元更換所守，檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Chong was ordered to exchange the territories he held with Chengyuan, and was appointed Acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was ordered to exchange posts with Chengyuan and was named acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 是歲，汴州節度使李願被三軍所逐，立都將李絺既為留後。

translations.literal: That year, Li Yuan, military governor of Bian Prefecture, was expelled by the three armies; the commander-in-chief Li Chi was established as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Bianzhou troops ousted Military Governor Li Yuan and installed Commander Li Chi as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以充久在汴州，從心悅附，命充為宣武節度使，兼統義成之師往討絺。

translations.literal: The court, because Chong had long been at Bian Prefecture and the men followed him willingly in attachment, ordered Chong to be Xuanwu military governor, also commanding the Yicheng army to march and punish Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chong had long served at Bian and the men were loyal to him, the court appointed him Xuanwu military governor and ordered him to lead the Yicheng troops against Chi.

sentences.zh: 會絺疽發腦，屬兵於紀綱李質。

translations.literal: It happened that Chi's carbuncle broke out in his brain; he entrusted the troops to the disciplinarian Li Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chi developed a carbuncle on his head and entrusted the troops to his senior staff officer Li Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質以計誅首亂，送絺歸京師。

translations.literal: Zhi by stratagem executed the chief rebel, and sent Chi back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi devised a plan to execute the ringleaders and sent Chi back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 充遂不戰而入大梁。

translations.literal: Chong then entered Great Liang without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chong entered the capital of the circuit, Daliang, without a fight.

sentences.zh: 時陳許李光顏亦奉詔討絺，軍於尉氏，意欲必先收汴，因大肆俘掠。

translations.literal: At that time Li Guangyan of Chen and Xu also received orders to punish Chi and encamped at Weishi, intending to seize Bian first, and therefore carried out wholesale capture and plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan of Chenxu had also been ordered against Chi and encamped at Weishi, intending to seize Bian first and consequently plundering the countryside freely.

sentences.zh: 汴州監軍使姚文壽亦欲招許下之師。

translations.literal: Yao Wenshou, the Bian Prefecture army supervisor, also wished to summon the Xu [Chenxu] forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wenshou, the Bianzhou army supervisor, also tried to draw in the Chenxu army.

sentences.zh: 充在中牟聞其謀，率眾徑至城下。

translations.literal: Chong at Zhongmou heard their plot and led his masses straight to below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this at Zhongmou, Chong marched straight to the city with his troops.

sentences.zh: 汴人素懷充來，皆踴躍相賀，無復疑貳。

translations.literal: The people of Bian had long yearned for Chong's coming; all leaped for joy and congratulated one another; there was no further doubt or divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Bian had long awaited Chong's arrival; they welcomed him with jubilation, and all doubts vanished.

sentences.zh: 詔加檢校司空。

translations.literal: An edict additionally appointed him Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of Works by edict.

sentences.zh: 詔割潁州隸滑州。

translations.literal: An edict carved off Ying Prefecture and subordinated it to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture was transferred by edict from Bian's jurisdiction to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 充既安堵，密籍部伍間，得嘗構惡者千余人。

translations.literal: After Chong had settled the people in peace, he secretly registered among the ranks and files, obtaining more than a thousand men who had once plotted evil.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, Chong quietly compiled a roll of the ranks and identified more than a thousand men who had previously stirred trouble.

sentences.zh: 一日下令，並父母妻子立出之，敢逡巡境內者斬！

translations.literal: One day he issued an order: together with parents, wives, and children they were immediately expelled; whoever dared linger within the borders would be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order one day expelling them together with their parents, wives, and children, on penalty of death for anyone who lingered within the circuit.

sentences.zh: 自是軍政大理，汴人無不愛戴。

translations.literal: From this the army and administration were greatly ordered; the people of Bian none failed to love and esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter military and civil administration were brought to good order, and the people of Bian came to esteem him universally.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，例加司徒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, by precedent he was additionally made Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year (824), he was promoted to Grand Minister by routine precedence.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，暴疾卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, he suddenly fell ill and died; he was then fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, he died of a sudden illness at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Minister; his posthumous name was Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Minister with the posthumous name Su ("Solemn").

sentences.zh: 充雖內外皆將家，素不事豪侈，常以簡約自持。

translations.literal: Although Chong was from a military family both within and without, he by nature did not pursue extravagance, and always maintained himself through simplicity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Though born into a military family on both sides, Chong never indulged in luxury and always held to a plain, restrained life.

sentences.zh: 臨機決策，動無遺悔，善將者多之。

translations.literal: Facing crises he decided policy; in action he left no regrets; many who were skilled generals praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He decided boldly in the moment and never looked back with regret; capable commanders widely praised him.

sentences.zh: 李質者，汴之牙將。

translations.literal: Li Zhi was a yamen guard general of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi was a staff guard officer at Bian.

sentences.zh: 李絺既為留後，倚質為心腹。

translations.literal: After Li Chi had become acting commander, he relied on Zhi as his intimate confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Chi became acting governor, he relied on Zhi as his closest confidant.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷以絺為郡守，誌邀節鉞，質勸喻不從。

translations.literal: When the court appointed Chi as prefect, Chi aspired to the commander's seal and staff; Zhi counseled and admonished, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the court named Chi a civil prefect, Chi still aspired to retain the commander's seal and staff; Zhi counseled him repeatedly, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 會絺疽發首，乃與監軍姚文壽謀，斬絺傳首京師。

translations.literal: When Chi's carbuncle broke out on his head, [Zhi] plotted with the army supervisor Yao Wenshou to behead Chi and transmit the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When a carbuncle broke out on Chi's head, Zhi plotted with Army Supervisor Yao Wenshou to kill Chi and send his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有詔以韓充鎮汴。

translations.literal: There was an edict appointing Han Chong to guard Bian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Han Chong military governor of Bian.

sentences.zh: 充未至，質權知軍州事。

translations.literal: Before Chong arrived, Zhi acted on authority to know army and prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chong arrived, Zhi served as acting military and civil governor.

sentences.zh: 使衙牙兵二千人，皆日給酒食，物力為之損屈。

translations.literal: The yamen guard troops, two thousand men, all received daily provisions of wine and food; material resources were thereby diminished and strained.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand yamen guard troops received daily rations of food and wine, draining the command's resources.

sentences.zh: 充將至，質曰：「若韓公始至，頓去二千人日膳，人情必大去；

translations.literal: When Chong was about to arrive, Zhi said: "If when Lord Han first arrives we suddenly remove the daily rations of two thousand men, human sentiment will greatly depart;
translations.idiomatic: As Chong's arrival neared, Zhi said, "If Lord Han arrives and suddenly cuts off daily rations for two thousand men, morale will collapse;

sentences.zh: 若不除之，後當無繼。

translations.literal: If we do not remove it, afterward there will be no means to continue.
translations.idiomatic: but if we do not end it, there will be no way to sustain it later.

sentences.zh: 不可留此弊以遺吾帥。」

translations.literal: We must not leave this abuse to bequeath to our commander."
translations.idiomatic: We cannot leave this abuse for our new commander to inherit."

sentences.zh: 遂處分停日膳而後迎充。

translations.literal: He then disposed matters, stopped the daily rations, and afterward welcomed Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the daily rations and then welcomed Chong in.

sentences.zh: 召為金吾將軍，長慶三年四月卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Gold Crow Guard general; in the fourth month of the third year of Changqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as a Gold Crow Guard general and died in the fourth month of the third year of Changqing (823).

sentences.zh: 王智興，字匡諫，懷州溫縣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was a native of Wen County in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing, styled Kuangjian, was a native of Wen County in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖靖，左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jing was General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jing served as general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 祖瑰，右金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui was general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 父縉，太子詹事。

translations.literal: His father Jin was Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin served as grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 智興少驍銳，為徐州衙卒，事刺史李洧。

translations.literal: Zhixing in youth was fierce and sharp; he was a Xu Prefecture yamen soldier and served Prefect Li Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhixing was bold and keen; he served as a Xu Prefecture yamen soldier under Prefect Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 及李納謀叛，欲害洧。

translations.literal: When Li Na plotted rebellion, he wished to kill Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na plotted rebellion, he sought Wei's life.

sentences.zh: 洧遂以徐州歸國。

translations.literal: Wei then submitted Xu Prefecture to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei thereupon submitted Xu Prefecture to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 納怒，以兵攻徐甚急。

translations.literal: Na in anger attacked Xu with troops very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Na pressed the siege of Xu with great force.
