sentences.zh: 智興健行，不四五日賫表京師求援。

translations.literal: Zhixing was a strong traveler; in no more than four or five days he carried memorials swiftly to the capital to seek relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing was a strong runner; within four or five days he carried memorials swiftly to the capital seeking relief.

sentences.zh: 德宗發朔方軍五千人隨智興赴之，淄青圍解。

translations.literal: Dezong dispatched five thousand Shuo-fang troops to follow Zhixing and go to their aid; the Zi-qing siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sent five thousand Shuo-fang troops with Zhixing to the rescue, and the Ziqing siege was broken.

sentences.zh: 自是，智興常以徐軍抗納，累歷滕、豐、沛、狄四鎮將。

translations.literal: From this, Zhixing constantly used the Xu army to resist Na, and successively served as garrison commander of the four posts Teng, Feng, Pei, and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zhixing led Xu troops against Na and in turn commanded the garrisons at Teng, Feng, Pei, and Di.

sentences.zh: 自是二十余年為徐將。

translations.literal: From this for more than twenty years he was a Xu commander.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years thereafter he served as a Xu commander.

sentences.zh: 元和中，王師誅吳元濟，李師道與蔡賊謀撓沮王師，頻出軍侵徐，徐帥李願以所部步騎悉委智興以抗之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe reign, the imperial army executed Wu Yuanji; Li Shidao with the Cai rebels plotted to thwart and discourage the imperial army, frequently sending out troops to invade Xu; the Xu commander Li Yuan entrusted all the infantry and cavalry under his command to Zhixing to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, after imperial forces killed Wu Yuanji, Li Shidao joined the Cai rebels in harassing the court's armies and repeatedly raided Xu; Military Governor Li Yuan put all his infantry and cavalry under Zhixing to repel them.

sentences.zh: 鄆將王朝晏以兵攻沛，智興擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Yan commander Wang Chaoyan attacked Pei with troops; Zhixing struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan commander Wang Chaoyan attacked Pei; Zhixing routed him.

sentences.zh: 賊又令姚海率勁兵二萬圍豐，攻城甚急。

translations.literal: The rebels again ordered Yao Hai to lead twenty thousand crack troops to besiege Feng; the assault on the city was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels next sent Yao Hai with twenty thousand elite troops to besiege Feng in a fierce assault.

sentences.zh: 智興復擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhixing again struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 於賊壁獲美妾，智興懼軍士爭之，乃曰：「軍中有女子，安得不敗？

translations.literal: At the rebel ramparts he captured a beautiful concubine; Zhixing feared the soldiers would quarrel over her, and therefore said: "When there are women in the army, how can one not be defeated?
translations.idiomatic: After capturing a beautiful woman in the enemy camp, Zhixing feared the troops would fight over her and said, "An army that keeps women cannot help but be defeated.

sentences.zh: 此雖無罪，違軍法也。」

translations.literal: Although this person is without guilt, it violates military law."
translations.idiomatic: Though she is innocent, this violates military law."

sentences.zh: 即斬之以徇。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded her to display.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded her on the spot as an example.

sentences.zh: 累官至侍御史、本軍都押衙。

translations.literal: He cumulatively reached the office of Palace Censor and Chief Superintendent of the Circuit Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace censor and chief superintendent of the circuit army.

sentences.zh: 十三年，王師誅李師道，智興率徐軍八千會諸道之師進擊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the imperial army executed Li Shidao; Zhixing led eight thousand Xu troops to join the armies of the various circuits in advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (818), after imperial forces killed Li Shidao, Zhixing led eight thousand Xu troops to join the allied armies in the advance.

sentences.zh: 與陳許之軍大破賊於金鄉，拔魚臺，俘斬萬計，以功遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: With the Chen and Xu armies he greatly defeated the rebels at Jinxiang, captured Yutai, and captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands; for merit he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: With the Chenxu army he routed the rebels at Jinxiang, took Yutai, and killed or captured tens of thousands; for this he was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授沂州刺史。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was appointed prefect of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，河朔復亂，征兵進討。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, Hebei again fell into disorder; troops were levied to advance and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing reign, Hebei erupted in rebellion again, and the court mobilized troops for a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 穆宗素知智興善將，遷檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，充武寧軍節度副使、河北行營都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Muzong had long known Zhixing was skilled as a general; he was transferred to Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently Censor Grandee, serving as Vice Military Governor of the Wuning Army and Chief Controller of Military Affairs for the Hebei Field Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, knowing Zhixing's skill as a commander, promoted him to acting left regular attendant and censor grandee, made him vice military governor of the Wuning Army, and named him chief controller of the Hebei field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，召智興以徐軍三千渡河，徐之勁卒皆在部下。

translations.literal: At first Zhixing was summoned to lead three thousand Xu troops across the river; Xu's crack soldiers were all under his command.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhixing was ordered to cross the river with three thousand Xu troops, bringing with him the circuit's best soldiers.

sentences.zh: 節度使崔群慮其旋軍難制，密表請追赴闕，授以他官。

translations.literal: Military Governor Cui Qun feared that when the army returned it would be hard to control; he secretly memorialized requesting that [Zhixing] be recalled to court and given another office.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Cui Qun feared Zhixing would be hard to control once his troops returned, and secretly memorialized the court to recall him and give him another post.

sentences.zh: 事未行，會赦王廷湊，諸道班師。

translations.literal: Before the matter could be carried out, there came an amnesty for Wang Tingcou; the various circuits withdrew their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be enacted, Wang Tingcou was pardoned and the allied armies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 智興先期入境，群頗憂疑，令府僚迎勞，且誡之曰：「兵士悉輸甲仗於外，副使以十騎入城。」

translations.literal: Zhixing beforehand entered the territory; Qun was quite worried and suspicious; he ordered his staff to welcome and console him, and also admonished him, saying: "All soldiers must surrender arms and armor outside; the vice commissioner shall enter the city with ten mounted escorts."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing entered the circuit ahead of his troops. Anxious and suspicious, Qun sent staff to welcome him and instructed: "All soldiers must deposit their arms outside the city; the vice governor may enter with only ten mounted escorts."

sentences.zh: 智興既首處，賓僚聞之心動，率歸師斬關而入，殺軍中異己者十余人。

translations.literal: Zhixing had already taken the foremost position; when the staff and guests heard this their hearts wavered; they led the returning army, cut through the gate and entered, and killed more than ten men in the army who were not of their own faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing had already taken the lead. When his officers heard Qun's instructions, they were incensed; they led the returning troops, forced the gates, and killed more than ten officers who opposed them.

sentences.zh: 然後詣衛謝群曰：「此軍情也。」

translations.literal: Afterward he went to the guard headquarters and apologized to Qun, saying: "This was the sentiment of the army."
translations.idiomatic: He then went to headquarters and apologized to Qun: "This was the will of the troops."

sentences.zh: 群治裝赴闕，智興遣兵士援送群家屬至埇橋。

translations.literal: Qun prepared his baggage and went to court; Zhixing sent soldiers to escort and convey Qun's family dependents to Yongqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Qun packed to leave for the capital; Zhixing sent troops to escort Qun's family as far as Yongqiao.

sentences.zh: 遂掠鹽鐵院緡幣及汴路進奉物，商旅貲貨，率十取七八。

translations.literal: He then plundered the Salt and Iron Commission's strings of cash and the tribute goods sent along the Bian route, and merchants' goods and valuables; on the whole he took seven or eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: He then plundered the salt and iron commission's funds, tribute goods bound for the capital along the Bian route, and merchants' cargo, taking seven or eight tenths of everything.

sentences.zh: 逐濠州刺史侯弘度。

translations.literal: He expelled Hou Hongdu, Prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He drove out Hou Hongdu, prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘度棄城走。

translations.literal: Hongdu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Hongdu abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以罷兵，力不能加討，遂授智興檢校工部尚書、徐州刺史、御史大夫，充武寧軍節度、徐泗濠觀察使。

translations.literal: The court, because the armies had been stood down and lacked the strength to punish further, thereupon appointed Zhixing Acting Minister of Works, Prefect of Xu Prefecture, and Censor Grandee, serving as Military Governor of the Wuning Army and Xu-Si-Hao Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With the armies stood down and unable to punish him by force, the court appointed Zhixing acting Minister of Works, prefect of Xu, and censor grandee, with full command as military governor of Wuning and commissioner over Xu, Si, and Hao.

sentences.zh: 自是智興務積財賄，以賂權勢，賈其聲譽，用度不足，稅泗口以裒益之。

translations.literal: From this Zhixing devoted himself to accumulating wealth and bribes to buy off the powerful, purchasing his reputation; when expenditures were insufficient, he taxed the Si Estuary to augment them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zhixing amassed wealth to bribe the powerful and buy reputation; when funds ran short, he levied taxes at the Si Estuary to make up the deficit.

sentences.zh: 累加至檢校僕射、司空。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively promoted to Acting Vice Director and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to acting vice director and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太和初，李同捷據滄德叛，智興上章，請躬督士卒討賊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Li Tongjie held Cang and De in rebellion; Zhixing submitted a memorial requesting to personally oversee the soldiers in punishing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign, Li Tongjie rebelled and held Cang and De; Zhixing memorialized the throne asking to lead the troops in person against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 乃出全軍三萬，自備五月糧餉，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: He then sent out the entire army of thirty thousand, himself supplying five months' provisions; the court praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with his full force of thirty thousand men and provisions for five months at his own expense; the court applauded the effort.

sentences.zh: 加檢校司徒、同平章事，兼滄德行營招撫使。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Acting Grand Minister, Associate Grand Councilor, and concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the Cangde Field Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting grand minister and associate grand councilor, and named pacification commissioner of the Cangde field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，同捷狂桀犯命，濟之以王廷湊，王師經年無功。

translations.literal: At first Tongjie was wild and defiant in offending orders; Ji Prefecture aided him together with Wang Tingcou; the imperial army for years had no success.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tongjie's defiance was sustained by aid from Ji and Wang Tingcou, and imperial campaigns had failed for years.

sentences.zh: 及智興拔棣州，賊大懼，諸軍稍務進取。

translations.literal: When Zhixing captured Di Prefecture, the rebels were greatly afraid; the various armies gradually devoted themselves to advancing and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixing captured Di Prefecture, the rebels were terrified and the allied armies began pressing forward in earnest.

sentences.zh: 以智興首功，加守太傅，封雁門郡王。

translations.literal: Because Zhixing had the chief merit, he was promoted to Defender Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For the leading share of the victory, he was made defender grand tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 賊平入朝，上賜宴麟德殿，賞賜珍玩名馬，進位侍中，改許州刺史、忠武軍節度、陳許蔡等州觀察使。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he entered court; the emperor bestowed a banquet at the Hall of Qilin Virtue, rewarded him with rare treasures and famous horses, advanced him to Palace Attendant, and changed him to Prefect of Xu Prefecture, military governor of the Zhongwu Army, and observation commissioner over Chen, Xu, Cai, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he went to court; the emperor feasted him at the Hall of Qilin Virtue, rewarded him with rare treasures and fine horses, promoted him to palace attendant, and transferred him to Xu Prefecture as military governor of Zhongwu and commissioner over Chen, Xu, Cai, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太和七年，改授河中尹、河中節度、晉磁隰觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe, he was transferred and appointed Prefect of Hezhong, military governor of Hezhong, and observation commissioner over Jin, Ci, Xi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe (833) he was reassigned as prefect of Hezhong, military governor of the Hezhong circuit, and commissioner over Jin, Ci, Xi, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 智興因入朝。

translations.literal: Zhixing thereupon entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing went to court on the transfer.

sentences.zh: 九年五月，改汴州刺史、宣武軍節度、宋亳汴潁觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year, he was changed to Prefect of Bian Prefecture, military governor of the Xuanwu Army, and observation commissioner over Song, Bo, Bian, Ying, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year (835) he was transferred to Bian as military governor of Xuanwu and commissioner over Song, Bo, Bian, Ying, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開成元年七月卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Kaicheng he died; he was seventy-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the first year of Kaicheng (836) at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，不視朝三日。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant; [the emperor] did not hold court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand commandant, and the emperor suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 葬於洛陽榆林之北原，四鎮將校會葬者千人。

translations.literal: He was buried on the north plain of Yulin in Luoyang; garrison commanders from the four posts attending the funeral numbered a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on the northern plain of Yulin outside Luoyang; a thousand garrison officers from his former commands attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 智興九子：晏平、晏宰、晏臯、晏實、晏恭、晏逸、晏深、晏斌、晏韜，而晏平、晏宰最知名。

translations.literal: Zhixing had nine sons: Yanping, Yanzai, Yangao, Yanshi, Yangong, Yanyi, Yanshen, Yanbin, and Yantao; of these Yanping and Yanzai were most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing had nine sons—Yanping, Yanzai, Yangao, Yanshi, Yangong, Yanyi, Yanshen, Yanbin, and Yantao—of whom Yanping and Yanzai were the best known.

sentences.zh: 晏平幼從父征伐，以討李同捷功，授檢校右散騎常侍、靈州大都督府長史、朔方靈鹽節度。

translations.literal: Yanping from youth followed his father on campaigns; for merit in punishing Li Tongjie he was appointed Acting Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Chief Administrator of the Great Protectorate Prefecture of Ling Prefecture, and military governor of Shuofang Ling and Salt.
translations.idiomatic: Yanping campaigned with his father from youth and, for his service against Li Tongjie, was appointed acting right regular attendant, chief administrator of the Lingzhou protectorate, and military governor of Shuofang Ling and Salt.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，奔歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Upon the mourning for his father, he rushed back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he rushed home to Luoyang for mourning.

sentences.zh: 晏平居官貪黷，去鎮日，擅將征馬四百余匹及兵仗七千事自衛，為憲司所糾。

translations.literal: Yanping in office was greedy and corrupt; on the day he left his post he arbitrarily took more than four hundred requisitioned horses and seven thousand sets of weapons and armor to guard himself, and was impeached by the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanping was corrupt in office; on leaving his post he took more than four hundred requisitioned horses and seven thousand weapons for his escort and was impeached by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 減死，長流康州。

translations.literal: Capital punishment was reduced; he was banished far to Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His sentence was reduced from death to permanent exile in Kang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以父喪，未赴流所，告於河北三鎮。

translations.literal: Because of his father's mourning, he did not proceed to the place of exile, but appealed to the three Hebei military governors.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his father's mourning, he failed to report to exile and appealed instead to the three Hebei commanders.

sentences.zh: 三帥上表救解，請從昭雪，改授撫州司馬。

translations.literal: The three commanders submitted memorials requesting rescue and release, asking that he be cleared and restored, and he was reassigned as Administrator of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: All three commanders memorialized the court to spare him and clear his name; he was reassigned instead as administrator of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋溫、薛廷老、盧弘宣封還制書，改永州司戶。

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Wei Wen, Xue Tinglao, and Lu Hongxuan sealed and returned the edict document; he was changed to Registrar of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants-in-Ordinary Wei Wen, Xue Tinglao, and Lu Hongxuan sealed and returned the edict; Yanping was reassigned as registrar of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋溫又執不下，文宗令中使宣諭方行。

translations.literal: Wei Wen again held firm and would not release it; Wenzong ordered a palace envoy to proclaim instructions before it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen again refused to release it until Emperor Wenzong sent a palace envoy with instructions.

sentences.zh: 晏宰於昆仲間最稱偉器，大中後，歷上黨、太原節度使。

translations.literal: Among his brothers Yanzai was most praised as a great vessel; after the Dazhong era he successively served as Military Governor of Shangdang and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Among the brothers Yanzai was regarded as the most capable; after the Dazhong reign he served in turn as military governor of Shangdang and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 扞回鶻、党項，屢立邊功。

translations.literal: He repelled the Uyghurs and Tangut, and repeatedly established frontier achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He repelled the Uyghurs and Tangut and won repeated victories on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 晏臯仕至左威衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yangao rose in office to General of the Left Majestic Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yangao rose to general of the Left Majestic Guard.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：於燕公以儒家子，逢時擾攘，不持士範，非義非俠，健者不為，末塗淪躓，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Duke Yan Yu, as a son of the Confucian school, encountered a time of turmoil, did not uphold the scholar's model, did what was neither righteous nor chivalrous—what the strong would not do—and in his final course stumbled and fell; this was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yu Di of Yan, a Confucian by training, lived in turbulent times yet abandoned the scholar's code, doing what was neither righteous nor brave; that he stumbled to ruin in the end was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 韓、王二帥，乘險蹈利，犯上無君，豺狼噬人，鵂鹠幸夜，爵祿過當，其可已乎？

translations.literal: The two commanders Han and Wang, seizing peril to tread profit, offending superiors without regard for their lord, wolves devouring men, owls prospering in the night—rank and salary beyond measure; can this be stopped?
translations.idiomatic: The commanders Han and Wang seized every advantage, defied their sovereign, preyed on the people like wolves, and flourished like owls in the dark—can such excessive honors ever be justified?

sentences.zh: 謂之功臣，恐多慚色。

translations.literal: To call them meritorious ministers—one fears there would be much to blush for.
translations.idiomatic: To call them meritorious servants of the state would be a blush upon the court itself.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：於子清狂，輕犯彜章。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yu's son was pure and wild, lightly violating constant law.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Yu Di was proud and reckless, lightly trampling the laws of the realm.

sentences.zh: 韓虐王剽，專恣一方。

translations.literal: Han was cruel, Wang was rapacious; each tyrannized a region alone.
translations.idiomatic: Han was cruel and Wang rapacious; each tyrannized his region alone.

sentences.zh: 元和赫斯，揮劍披攘。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era authority was august; swords were brandished and obstacles swept aside.
translations.idiomatic: Under the august Yuanhe reign, the court brandished the sword and swept rebellion aside.

sentences.zh: 擇肉之倫，爪距摧藏。

translations.literal: The breed that chooses flesh—talons and spurs were broken and hidden away.
translations.idiomatic: Those beasts that fed on the realm had their claws and spurs broken at last.
